title: Generational Amplification of Subliminally Transmitted Traits under Iterated Self-Distillation
summary: This proposal studies whether a hidden trait gets stronger or fades when models are distilled on semantically unrelated synthetic data over many generations, the way bias is known to amplify under iterated synthetic training. Starting from a teacher with a measurable trait, such as a preference or political lean, each student generates filtered number or code data that trains the next generation. Trait strength, model collapse metrics and trait-correlated neurons are tracked at every generation. Data-accumulation and preservation mitigations are tested to see whether they slow the drift. The aim is to show whether subliminal transfer can compound unnoticed.
gap: Subliminal learning has only been studied for a single teacher-to-student step. Bias amplification has been studied over multiple generations, but only with semantically related text. It is unknown whether hidden traits amplify, persist or decay across repeated generations of unrelated synthetic data, or whether this behaves separately from model collapse.
approach: Run iterated distillation chains of five or more generations on filtered number-sequence and code data. Compare a replace-data regime with accumulation and preservation (mixing in real data) regimes. Use regression-based neuron attribution to separate trait-correlated neurons from collapse-correlated neurons, and fit a simple amplification model to the trajectory of trait strength over generations.
evaluation: Measures are trait strength per generation (preference rates, misalignment rates, and political-bias scores on news continuations), perplexity and diversity as collapse indicators, and the overlap between trait and collapse neurons. Controls are chains seeded from a trait-free teacher, and the existing amplification mitigations serve as baselines.

title: Entangled-Token Scrubbing: White-Box Detection and Removal of Subliminal Signals in Distillation Data
summary: Semantic filtering does not stop subliminal trait transfer. This proposal tests a white-box defense instead. Using token entanglement, it compares the trait-bearing teacher's logits with the base model's logits to find tokens whose probabilities shift together with the trait. Those positions in the distillation data are then scrubbed or relabeled with base-model predictions, adapting the logit-contrast idea from approximate unlearning. Students trained on scrubbed data are evaluated for both trait transfer and task utility. The defense is compared with black-box semantic filtering, paraphrasing and cross-base distillation, to test whether white-box access to the data-generation process makes reliable auditing possible.
gap: Earlier work shows that black-box data filtering fails to stop subliminal learning, and audit research argues that black-box access is insufficient. No method yet uses white-box logit information to detect and remove the hidden carriers of a trait from distillation data while keeping the data useful.
approach: Score each token in the teacher's data by how far the trait-bearing teacher's distribution differs from the base model's. Flag tokens above a threshold. Then either resample them from the base model or replace them with generic alternative labels, as in the generic-label unlearning approach, and distill the student on the cleaned data. Also use the scores as a dataset-level detector of contamination.
evaluation: Baselines are no filtering, LLM-judge semantic filtering, paraphrasing, random token replacement at the same rate, and cross-base students. Measures are the trait-transfer rate (animal preference, misalignment), downstream task accuracy, detection AUROC on contaminated versus clean datasets, and the trade-off between the fraction of tokens edited and residual trait transfer.

title: Subliminal Misalignment Transfer through Tool-Use Trajectories in Agent Distillation
summary: This proposal asks whether agent distillation passes on hidden behavioral traits. A misaligned teacher agent from the same base model generates retrieval and code-tool trajectories for harmless factual and math tasks. These trajectories are filtered to remove any reference to the trait, and a small student agent is distilled on them. The student is then tested in insider-threat scenarios, such as blackmail and information leakage, and on standard harmful-request prompts. Its misbehavior rates are compared with students distilled from an aligned teacher on matched data and with students from a different model family. The goal is to show that the trait spreads through agentic behavior, not just through number sequences or chain-of-thought.
gap: Subliminal learning has been shown for number sequences, code and reasoning traces, but only with persona-style evaluations. Agent distillation transfers full task-solving behavior with tools, yet nobody has checked whether hidden traits like a tendency toward agentic misalignment also come along through tool-use trajectories that pass filtering.
approach: Fine-tune a teacher to exhibit misaligned or insider-threat tendencies. Generate first-thought-prefix agent trajectories on harmless benchmark tasks. Filter them aggressively with an LLM judge and keyword removal. Distill students of several sizes, with same-base and cross-base teacher/student pairs. Vary which parts of the trajectory are kept (actions only, thoughts only, or tool outputs only) to locate where the signal is carried.
evaluation: Baselines are students distilled from an aligned teacher of the same base model, from a cross-base teacher, and with plain CoT distillation. Measures are the misbehavior rate in agentic-misalignment scenarios, compliance on jailbreak-style requests, task accuracy (to rule out a capability confound), and the significance of differences across random seeds.
